info.title: mConsent API
info.description:
**mConsent** provides unified consent management across the platform - communication preferences, data-sharing permissions, and feature-level opt-ins - with org-configurable consent policies. ## What this service does - **Communication Consent** - Manages permission to contact users via specific channels (email, sms, push) for marketing, transactional, or operational purposes. - **Data-Sharing Consent** - Controls whether a user's data can be collected, processed, or shared for analytics (wearable-data, clinical-data). - **Feature Consent** - Manages opt-in for specific product features that process user data (AI coaching, health reports, nudges). - **Organization Consent Policies** - Org-level configuration defining which consents are required, optional, or disabled for members. - **Immutable Consent History** - Consent records are never deleted; revocation sets status and timestamp for full audit trail. ## Conventions - All successful JSON responses wrap results under a top-level `data` property. - OAuth2 scopes gate admin/system/user operations (see **Security Schemes**). - IDs are strings; timestamps are ISO-8601 date-times with UTC `Z` (e.g., `2026-03-12T14:30:00Z`). ## Notes - mConsent replaces consent functionality previously embedded in mPO. See migration plan in requirements documentation. - Consent records are immutable - revocation sets `status: revoked` and `revokedAt` timestamp. Records are never physically deleted. - Organization consent policies control onboarding flow and feature availability per org.

Repository

post.description:
Grants a consent record for the specified user. The consent is created with `status: active`.

If an active consent already exists for the same `userId + category + scope` combination
(and `channel` for communication consents), the request is idempotent and returns the
existing consent record with a `200` response.

The `version` field records the consent policy version the user agreed to at the time of grant.

200.description: Consent already exists (idempotent) - returns existing active consent

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of consent records for the specified user.
Supports filtering by category, scope, channel, and status.

Default status filter is `active` - to see revoked consents or full history, set `status=revoked` or `status=all`.

UserSecurity callers can only list their own consents. SystemSecurity callers can list any user's consents.

**Service-to-service consent checks:** Use query filters to verify consent status.
For example, `GET /users/{userId}/consents?category=data-sharing&scope=wearable-data&status=active`
returns an empty list if the user has not consented.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by scope within the category (e.g., `marketing`, `wearable-data`, `ai-coaching`)

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Filter by contact channel (only applicable for `communication` category): `email`, `sms`, `push`

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by consent status. Default: `active`. Use `all` to include revoked consents.

count.description: Total number of matching consents (omitted when using startAfter)

nextPageUrl.description: URL for the next page of results (null when no more pages)

get.description:
Returns a single consent record by ID. Includes full consent details
regardless of status (active or revoked).

delete.description:
Revokes an active consent by setting `status: revoked` and recording the `revokedAt` timestamp.
The consent record is **not deleted** - it remains for audit history.

Attempting to revoke a consent that is linked to a `required` consent policy returns `403 Forbidden`.
Revoking an already-revoked consent returns `200` with the existing revoked record (idempotent).

Emits a `consent.revoked` event to Kinesis for downstream consumers (Analytics Consumer, Notification Service).

example.title: Forbidden
example.message: Cannot revoke required consent. The consent policy for data-sharing:wearable-data is set to required by your organization.

post.description:
Creates a consent policy for the specified organization. Policies define whether a consent
scope is `required`, `optional`, or `disabled` for the org's members.

- `required` - Members must grant this consent during onboarding. Cannot proceed without it.
- `optional` - Members can grant or revoke at any time. Shown during onboarding with `defaultValue`.
- `disabled` - Consent scope is not available for this org. Not shown during onboarding.

Returns `409 Conflict` if a policy already exists for the same `orgId + category + scope`.

example.description: Allow your anonymized wearable and sleep data to contribute to organization-level analytics dashboards.

data.description: Allow your anonymized wearable and sleep data to contribute to organization-level analytics dashboards.

get.description:
Returns all consent policies for the specified organization.
Supports filtering by category and scope.

UserSecurity callers can view policies for their own org (used during onboarding to display available consents).
AdminSecurity callers can view policies for any org.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by scope within the category

data.description: Allow your anonymized wearable and sleep data to contribute to organization-level analytics dashboards.
Required notifications for account activity and security alerts.
Enable personalized AI-powered sleep coaching and recommendations.

put.description:
Updates an existing consent policy. The `version` field is auto-incremented on each update.

Changing `requirement` from `optional` to `required` does not retroactively revoke existing opt-outs
- it applies to new members going forward. Existing members are prompted to grant consent on next app visit.

Changing `requirement` to `disabled` does not revoke existing consents - it hides the scope from
onboarding and stops new grants.

example.description: Required for participation in the wellness program. Your anonymized data contributes to organization-level health analytics.

data.description: Required for participation in the wellness program. Your anonymized data contributes to organization-level health analytics.

delete.description:
Removes a consent policy from the organization. This does not revoke existing consents
granted under this policy - it only removes the policy definition.

After deletion, the consent scope is no longer shown during onboarding and no new consents
can be granted for this scope in this org.

Consent.description: A consent record representing a user's permission for a specific category and scope

userId.description: mID account ID of the consenting user

category.description: Consent category: `communication` (contact channel permissions), `data-sharing` (data collection/processing permissions), or `feature` (product feature opt-ins)

status.description: Current consent status: `active` (consent granted) or `revoked` (consent withdrawn)

revokedAt.description: When consent was revoked (null if still active)

version.description: Consent policy version at time of grant (tracks which T&C version the user agreed to)

value.description: Contact address or handle (only present for `communication` category, e.g., email address, phone number)

NewConsent.description: Request body for granting a new consent

version.description: Consent policy version the user is agreeing to

value.description: Contact address or handle (required for `communication` category)

ConsentPolicy.description: An organization-level consent policy defining requirements for a specific consent scope

orgId.description: Organization ID this policy belongs to

category.description: Consent category this policy applies to

scope.description: Scope within the category this policy applies to

requirement.description: Requirement level: `required` (must grant, cannot revoke), `optional` (user choice), `disabled` (not available)

defaultValue.description: Default consent state for new members (only meaningful for `optional` policies)

displayName.description: Human-readable name shown during onboarding consent flow

description.description: Explanation shown to the user during onboarding
description.example: Allow your anonymized wearable and sleep data to contribute to organization-level analytics dashboards.

NewConsentPolicy.description: Request body for creating a new consent policy

defaultValue.description: Default consent state for new members (only meaningful for `optional` policies)
